source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Electrical, p.6Y-19

procedures.title: Breakerless (transistor) ignition: maintenance
steps: A test tachometer can be connected to the primary circuit as on a conventional system, but first confirm with the instrument supplier that it reads correctly and will not damage the breakerless system.

procedures.title: Ignition coil (breakerless): check
steps: Primary: put an ohmmeter across the 2 primary terminals; expect .35 to .55 ohm at 75°F. Infinite means open (an intermittent open can cause a run-but-miss condition).

Secondary: read from the high-tension center tower to either primary terminal, on a scale with 20,000 ohms in or near its middle third; expect 8,000 to 12,500 ohms at 75°F. Infinite means the secondary is open.
If using a coil tester, follow its maker's procedure and make sure it can test this special coil.

procedures.title: Spark plugs: tune-up service
steps: At tune-up, remove, inspect, clean and regap the plugs; replace bad ones (see Spark Plugs service).

procedures.title: Distributor contact points: clean
steps: Dress dirty points with a few strokes of a clean, fine-cut contact file kept only for this job and free of grease.
Only remove scale or dirt; do not try to file away all roughness or make the faces smooth.
Replace badly burned or pitted points and find the cause.
notes: Dull-looking points after long use may still work fine.
Oxidized points come from high resistance or loose condenser circuit connections, oil or dirt on contacts, wrong adjustment, or high voltage.
Pitting indicates an unbalanced ignition system, often too much or too little condenser capacity.
